_comment: Ground truth transcribed from the published DFTT answer keys. Sizes and MD5s are as documented by the test authors; offsets are the byte offset of the file's header within the image, measured against the image itself. 'recoverable' is false where the file is deliberately corrupted or is not a type TRACE carves.

dfrws-2006-challenge.raw.title: DFRWS 2006 Carving Challenge (raw, no filesystem)
dfrws-2006-challenge.raw.note: 32 files in 22 deliberately awkward scenarios. There is no filesystem, so the whole image is carved. Several scenarios target carving heuristics directly: 3c plants 0xFFD8 in the sector before a JPEG, 3j plants a sector beginning 0xFFD9 inside one.

false_positives_to_avoid.note: scenario 3c: a lone sector starting 0xFFD8, no image

dfrws-2007-challenge.img.title: DFRWS 2007 Carving Challenge (raw, no filesystem)
dfrws-2007-challenge.img.note: The 2007 challenge deepened 2006: more file types and more complex fragmentation. Every planted file of a type TRACE carves is listed, transcribed from challenge-file-info.txt (size, MD5) and challenge-layout.txt (fragments) in the official repository; ZIP is not, as only its embedded members are documented.
